months.name: January
months.summary: Rapid vegetative growth phase across Malawi. High weed competition and top-dressing fertiliser window.
reminders: Apply Urea / CAN top-dressing on maize at knee-height (21-28 days after planting).
Conduct thorough first and second weeding before weeds set seed.
Scout early mornings for Fall Armyworm (FAW) egg masses and funnel leaf damage.
Ensure drainage furrows are open in low-lying fields to prevent waterlogging.

districtAdvisories.Southern: High humidity in Shire Valley and Thyolo; monitor tomato late blight and maize stalk borer.
districtAdvisories.Central: Peak top-dressing period across Lilongwe, Kasungu and Dedza. Apply Urea on moist soil.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Lakeside and upland rains steady; maintain terracing and contour bunds in hilly terrain.

months.name: February
months.summary: Maize tasseling and cob formation, groundnut pegging, and pulse flowering across all regions.
reminders: Do not weed or cultivate around groundnuts once pegging begins to protect young pods.
Apply second split of nitrogen top-dressing on late-planted or long-season cereal varieties.
Scout for grain borers and fungal leaf spots (Grey Leaf Spot / Turcicum blight).
Bank ridges and construct contour swales to prevent severe soil erosion during heavy downpours.

districtAdvisories.Southern: Green maize harvesting begins in early-planted lowlands (Chikwawa, Nsanje, Mangochi).
districtAdvisories.Central: Maize cob filling in progress; keep field perimeters clear of tall bush to deter wild pests.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Peak weeding for late-planted rice in Karonga and Nkhatabay irrigation schemes.

months.name: March
months.summary: Grain filling, starch accumulation, and early pulse maturation. Preparing for drying and storage.
reminders: Harvest early maturing pulses, cowpeas, and green maize for household consumption.
Inspect mature groundnut pods by checking internal pod shell browning (70-75% brown indicates maturity).
Begin repairing granaries, nkhokwe, and ventilated drying cribs.
Prepare clean tarpaulins, drying mats, and purchase hermetic grain storage bags (PICS bags).

districtAdvisories.Southern: Groundnut lifting commences in early planted areas; avoid damp stacking to prevent aflatoxin.
districtAdvisories.Central: Maize dent stage in Lilongwe and Mchinji; allow stalks to begin natural field drydown.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Steady rice heading in Lakeside schemes; regulate water levels to ensure uniform grain fill.

months.name: April
months.summary: Rainfall tapers off across most of Malawi. Main crop harvest begins for legumes and early maize.
reminders: Harvest mature groundnuts immediately to avoid sprouting and pod detachment in drying ground.
Stook or bend maize cobs downward to shed late rains and deter bird attack.
Dry harvested grains on raised platforms or clean sheets, never directly on bare wet soil.
Collect crop residues for composting or livestock fodder rather than burning them.

districtAdvisories.Southern: Main maize harvest underway; transport dry cobs to secure storage to avoid field theft.
districtAdvisories.Central: Soybean pod maturity reaches 90%; harvest early morning to avoid pod shatter losses.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Cooler temperatures arriving in high plateaus (Misuku, Viphya); prepare seed potato stores.

months.name: May
months.summary: Peak national harvest month. Shelling, drying, moisture testing, and commercial marketing.
reminders: Dry grain thoroughly until moisture is below 13.5% (use salt-bottle test or moisture meter).
Treat clean grain with approved grain protectant dust or store in airtight hermetic bags.
Keep records of total bags harvested, household consumption needs, and marketable surplus.
Check district market price boards (Ulimi wa Malawi Market Centre) before selling to traders.

districtAdvisories.Southern: Cotton picking begins in Shire Valley; sort clean white seed cotton from stained locks.
districtAdvisories.Central: Central region tobacco auction floors active; assemble certified legume seed stocks.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Rice harvesting in full swing in Karonga and Salima borders.

months.name: June
months.summary: Cool dry winds arrive. Main rainfed harvest completes; winter dimba farming commences.
reminders: Prepare dambo wetlands and irrigated beds for dry-season horticulture and winter maize.
Fence vegetable gardens against roaming goats and cattle.
Store agricultural produce off the floor on timber pallets with 50cm wall clearance.
Deworm livestock and construct elevated predator-proof poultry and goat kholas.

districtAdvisories.Southern: Bvumbwe and Thyolo nursery beds established for cool-season brassicas and tomatoes.
districtAdvisories.Central: Dedza and Ntcheu winter Irish potato planting in valley bottoms (dambos).
districtAdvisories.Northern: Construct firebreaks around woodlots, orchards, and perennial coffee fields.

months.name: July
months.summary: Coldest month in Malawi. Active irrigation farming in valley bottoms and lakeside schemes.
reminders: Water dimba crops early morning to reduce cold shock and evening fungal dampness.
Incorporate organic manure and compost into horticultural beds.
Scout tomato nursery beds for early signs of red spider mites and blight.
Monitor stored grains in nkhokwe for weevil activity and ensure roofs are leak-free.

districtAdvisories.Southern: Frost caution in high-elevation pockets (Mulanje, Dedza borders); mulch sensitive seedlings.
districtAdvisories.Central: High market demand in Lilongwe for fresh tomatoes, cabbages, and onions.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Lakeside irrigation schemes active along Lake Malawi shorelines.

months.name: August
months.season: Dry Season / Nyengo Ya Chilimwe Yowuma
months.summary: Warming weather; peak dry-season vegetable marketing and early land preparation planning.
reminders: Maintain irrigation channels, treadle pump seals, and solar pump filters.
Harvest winter Irish potatoes in Ntcheu and Dedza.
Review last season's input costs, crop yields, and financial returns.
Begin sourcing certified seed and basal fertiliser early to avoid pre-season price spikes.

districtAdvisories.Southern: Prepare land early in the Lower Shire before intense heat builds up.
districtAdvisories.Central: High tomato yields arriving from Linthipe and Bwanje valley irrigators.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Misuku hills coffee harvesting, pulping, and wet fermentation.

months.name: September
months.season: Hot Dry Season / Dzuwa ndi Kutentha
months.summary: Hot, dry conditions. Active field clearing, ridge reforming, and compost distribution.
reminders: Clear fields and align old crop residues along ridge contours; avoid burning residues.
Distribute well-rotted livestock manure and compost into planting stations.
Deep-till hardpan layers to improve rainwater infiltration during upcoming rains.
Prune fruit trees (mangoes, citrus, macadamia) and clear base tree basins.

districtAdvisories.Southern: Intense heat in Chikwawa/Nsanje; ensure shade and clean water for all livestock.
districtAdvisories.Central: Tobacco seedbeds established under grass thatch covers in Lilongwe and Kasungu.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Check terracing and water-catchment structures across Mzimba and Chitipa hills.

months.name: October
months.summary: Hottest month in Malawi. Final input procurement, certified seed verification, and ridge completion.
reminders: Finalize all ridge making, box ridging, and planting basin construction.
Test seed germination (soak 100 seeds in damp cloth for 5 days; >90% should sprout).
Purchase certified basal fertiliser (23:10:5+6S) and legume inoculants.
Construct water absorption bunds (swales) to trap early seasonal rainwater.

districtAdvisories.Southern: Occasional early showers (Chidzimalole) may occur; do not plant on dry soil until effective rain falls.
districtAdvisories.Central: Ensure all planting ridges are 75cm apart with tied ridges every 2-3 meters.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Sort certified sweet potato vines and disease-free cassava cuttings.

months.name: November
months.season: Onset of Main Rains / Chiyambi cha Mvula
months.summary: Rainy season commences. Planting window opens with first effective rains (≥25-30mm).
reminders: Do not plant until rain penetrates the soil at least 25-30 cm deep.
Plant certified maize, groundnuts, and soybean within 48 hours of effective rainfall.
Apply basal fertiliser (23:10:5+6S) at planting or within 7 days of crop emergence.
Re-plant missing stations (gap-filling) within 7 days of emergence to maintain plant density.

districtAdvisories.Southern: Rains often start first in Southern Highlands; plant immediately as soil reaches field capacity.
districtAdvisories.Central: Central Plain planting begins; watch soil moisture depth across Lilongwe and Dowa.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Rain onset typically late November to early December; maintain seed readiness.

months.name: December
months.season: Full Planting & Early Weeding / Kulima ndi Kusalira
months.summary: Nationwide planting completion, nursery transplanting for rice and tobacco, and first weeding.
reminders: Complete all late cereal and legume planting by mid-December for optimal yield.
Conduct first weeding 10-14 days after crop emergence to eliminate early weed competition.
Inspect seedling roots and leaves for cutworms, grasshoppers, and early armyworm.
Prepare Urea top-dressing fertilizer for January application.

districtAdvisories.Southern: Scout for stalk borers in young maize stands; consult local AEDO for approved controls.
districtAdvisories.Central: Transplant tobacco seedlings into prepared ridges; apply basal compound fertilizer.
districtAdvisories.Northern: Rice seedbed transplanting in Karonga and Nkhotakota wetland paddies.

cropTimelines.name: Chimanga (Maize - Hybrid / OPV)
cropTimelines.ecology: All agro-ecological zones (Lowland, Medium & High Plateau)

stages.notes: Clear residues, construct 75cm ridges, build tied-ridges every 2m.
Plant 1 seed per hole at 25cm station spacing. Apply 23:10:5+6S (4 bags/ha).
Scout for Fall Armyworm funnels; hand-weed stations.
Apply Urea (4 bags/ha) in moist soil, 5-10cm away from stalk.
Ensure good drainage; avoid weed competition.
Dry to <13.5% moisture; treat with grain protectant or store in PICS bags.
Prepare deep, loose, well-drained ridges to facilitate peg penetration.
Plant double rows per 75cm ridge, 15cm between stations, 1 seed per hole.
Keep weed-free during initial establishment.
CRITICAL: Stop all hoed weeding once pegging starts to avoid cutting pegs.
Lift pods when 70% of inner shells turn dark brown; dry pods on clean racks.

cropTimelines.name: Soya (Soybean - Tikolore, Makwacha)
cropTimelines.ecology: Medium to high altitude with reliable rainfall (Kasungu, Dowa, Dedza)

stages.notes: Mix seed with Rhizobium bio-fertiliser inoculant in shade using sugar-water slurry.
Plant double rows on ridges, 5-7cm apart in continuous drill.
Weed twice before crop canopy closes; scout for caterpillars.
Ensure soil moisture; monitor for red leaf blotch or rust.
Harvest when 90% of leaves drop and pods rattle; harvest early morning to prevent shattering.

cropTimelines.name: Mpunga (Kilombero / Faya / Nunkile)
cropTimelines.ecology: Lakeside plains (Salima, Karonga, Nkhotakota) and Shire Valley schemes

stages.notes: Prepare raised nursery beds near reliable water source.
Puddle paddy soil to form impervious mud layer.
Transplant 2-3 seedlings per hill at 20cm x 20cm spacing.
Maintain 5cm water level; top dress with Urea at tillering and panicle initiation.
Drain field 10 days before harvest; cut golden panicles and thresh on tarpaulin.

cropTimelines.name: Chinangwa (Cassava - Manyokola, Sauti)
cropTimelines.ecology: Lakeside districts (Nkhata Bay, Nkhotakota) and Southern lowlands

stages.notes: Select healthy, disease-free stems 25-30cm long with 4-6 nodes.
Plant cuttings slanting at 45 degrees or horizontally 10cm deep, 1m apart.
Uproot and destroy any plants showing mosaic distortion or leaf curl.
Roots expand underground; maintain ridges to prevent exposure to sun and pests.
Harvest progressively as needed or in bulk for commercial starch/flour processing.

cropTimelines.name: Tomato (Fresh Vegetable - Heinz, Rodade)
cropTimelines.ecology: Valley bottoms, irrigated schemes, and protected beds nationwide

stages.notes: Fine soil, light shade netting, drench with fungicide to prevent damping off.
Transplant vigorous seedlings in evening; incorporate compost & basal fertiliser.
Tie vines to sturdy stakes to keep foliage off moist soil and improve airflow.
Apply CAN every 2-3 weeks; pinch out bottom suckers.
Pick fruit at breaker or pink stage for distance markets; handle gently in crates.
